minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved its FY17 sewer budget and set a Feb 29 workshop on grease trap rules.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed the sewer debt and betterment projections, then approved the FY17 operating budget. It discussed Town Meeting warrant items, a change process for regulations, and the grease trap program, including a Small Water proposal and disputed invoices. It also covered the Highfield Village sewer pipe, Town Caucus openings, and the prior minutes.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted on the FY17 sewer budget after reviewing debt service and betterment income; the minutes record the vote as not audible.
A workshop on grease trap rules was set for Monday the 29th at 4 at the highway department.
The commission will request a cost quote from Small Water for the grease trap monitoring proposal.
The pump station operations and maintenance contract is to be prepared for competitive bid.
Members objected to a Small Water grease trap invoice and said the Weston and Sampson fee study firm should do no more work.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates and betterment bills depend on how debt service is covered, and retained earnings were to cover the gap until older debt falls off.
Grease trap rules, monitoring costs and a regulation change process could change requirements and fees for food businesses and sewer users, and a warrant article could come to a Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: The grease trap workshop on Monday the 29th at 4 at the highway department.
The Small Water cost quote and further workshops on a regulation change process for a possible warrant article.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the $77,000 Town Meeting transfer, the 2% projection, the $5,000 Weston and Sampson limit and the regulation workshops, but each has many items the other lacks. The main thing to know is that our record could not hear the FY17 budget vote, which the official minutes say passed unanimously, and that the grease trap and contract decisions differ between the two.
